title: System design
audience: a computer science graduate or an experienced self-taught programmer preparing for and starting a software engineering job
purpose: Design large-scale systems as in industry and interviews: requirements and constraints, back-of-the-envelope estimation, load balancing and horizontal scaling, caching, replication and sharding, SQL and NoSQL data modeling, queues and asynchronous processing, consistency and idempotency, worked designs of common systems, reliability, rate limiting and observability.
primary_reading: The System Design Primer (free, on GitHub)

weeks.1: The system design process: requirements and constraints
weeks.5: Databases at scale: replication and sharding
weeks.6: SQL versus NoSQL, and data modeling
weeks.9: Designing a URL shortener and a news feed
weeks.11: Reliability: redundancy, rate limiting and graceful degradation
weeks.12: Observability and running systems in production

blocks.deliverable: Estimate storage and traffic for three systems.
Choose a caching strategy for a read-heavy service.
Week 7 midterm; design a job-processing pipeline.
Write a full design for one system.
Write service-level objectives and a runbook for a design.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Design dossier: write complete designs for two supplied systems (for example a ride-sharing dispatch service and a photo-sharing service) with requirements, estimates, diagrams described in text, data models, API sketches, and scaling and failure analysis, plus a written mock-interview walkthrough.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
